messages:
maya: Hey — PR CI keeps flaking when we run quantization evals. GH Actions times out on model download or the runner OOMs. Anyone else seen this?

devin: yup saw a couple yesterday. heavy evals shouldn't be on GH Actions. we should do a lightweight presubmit and push full runs to buildkite or nightly.

sam: Agreed. Proposed split: 
- presubmit: `eval-smoke` (fast, 5-10s, checks runtime + pass/fail)
- postmerge/nightly: `eval-full` (quantize variants, multiple seeds, metrics)

jordana: Also a bug in eval-runner: we weren't fixing RNG seed for the quantized runs so metric variance looks worse than it is. I'll open a PR to set `np.random.seed` + torch manual seed.

maya: nice catch @jordana. for infra: GH Actions is limited on memory and ephemeral download speed. buildkite or our dedicated agents are better for model-heavy jobs.

buildkite-bot: Buildkite job 48291 failed on agent 'g4dn-large' due to no available agents, queued for 12m then cancelled.

devin: we should tag agents and prioritize eval-full on a separate pool. Use tag `eval-heavy` so it doesn't steal capacity from other infra.

sam: Also can we cache model artifacts? Docker layer caching isn't shared across GH hosted runners. For buildkite we can upload model weights to S3 and use a small checksum file. Example: 
```
# download cached weights
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-eval-cache/models/llama-13B-q8/checksum.txt .
if [ -f checksum.txt ]; then aws s3 cp s3://redwood-eval-cache/models/llama-13B-q8/model.tar.gz ./; fi
```

jordana: Another CI tweak: add an `eval-metadata.yml` in the repo (metric lockfile) with baseline numbers. PR gating can compare new run to baseline and only block if regression > threshold. Keeps gating deterministic.

maya: How do we handle quantize experiment permutations? like q4_q5 different kernels. Running all in presubmit is impossible.

devin: presubmit runs a small subset: canonical fp16 + one quantized variant (q8), and smoke microbench. full sweep runs nightly. also add an explicit `--quick` flag to the runner that reduces examples and seq len.

sam: For GitHub Actions workflow snippet, something like: 
```
name: Eval-smoke
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: pytest tests/evals/test_smoke.py --maxfail=1 -q
```

maya: For Buildkite pipeline: use agents with `agent: "queue=eval-heavy"` and enable artifact upload to s3. Also add `retry` on transient network failures.

buildkite-bot: Note: make sure to rotate the CI token used to download private weights. token `EVAL_DL_TOKEN` will expire 2026-04-01.

jordana: PR opened: `eng-ml#724` fixes seed + adds `--quick` flag to eval-runner. also added a small unit test for determinism.

devin: action items: 
- maya: add GH Actions `eval-smoke` workflow and require it on PRs (non-blocking for perf-only docs).
- sam: set up S3 artifact bucket + small wrapper to cache model downloads.
- jordana: land seed fix and add metric-lockfile writer.
- maya+devin: coordinate Buildkite `eval-full` pipeline + agent tagging.

maya: timeline? can we have smoke checks in 2 days and move heavy to nightly by EOW?

sam: 2 days for smoke workflow + S3 bucket shallow setup. nightly pipeline by Fri if agents are available.

ci-bot: scheduled job 1763585600 (nightly-eval) created, will run full sweep at 04:00 UTC next night.

maya: Thanks team. we'll mark PRs with `eval:needs-smoke` until workflows are in. :thumbsup:

jordana: FYI: small perf note — use `docker build --cache-from` on our buildkite images to reduce layers pulled on agent start. fixed in my local branch.

devin: if flakiness persists after these changes we'll add a retry wrapper around model download + exponential backoff.

maya: perfect. assigning owners in the ticket.

sam: moving quantize sweeps to nightly will also reduce CI cost. win-win.

maya: closing loop here. ping if you hit blockers. :rocket:
